doc.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Family, children and their view of his work
summary: He has six children between him and his wife, did not push music on them, and they simply saw Dad going off to work.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Do you have a family? Children?
Yeah. I have, my wife and I combined it’s not our first marriage for either — and we have six children between us and grandchildren. So we have a pretty widespread family now.
Are there musicians in the family?

No. Actually I have a grandson right now who seems to have probably some interest but it’s too soon to tell. But I never encouraged it. I knew how hard it was, and I never pushed music and I really think that if — I’m sure the same would be true of acting or any of the arts, if a child is determined to do it, they’ll do it no matter what you tell them. And if they don’t have that determination they probably shouldn’t do it. So there’s really, you know the whole subject of encouragement I think is a difficult one.
Right. Do you think they had a sense, your children, of what you did for a living? Did they understand it? Did they think it was a little out of the ordinary?

You know that’s an interesting question, Monk, I’ve never really thought of it that way. A couple of my older kids when they were still little actually I would take on, for instance, studio calls with me, just to see if they would find that interesting, and like what did you do at the office today. And they always seemed to enjoy it, that sort of thing. But generally I’d say no. I think Dad just went off to do what he does. I’m not sure—
Right. Kids take it in stride. Do you have a gig tonight? — I remember my own little kids saying that at a very early age. “Dad, you got a gig tonight?” You were just going to work.
